cards.power: Epistemic Sabotage – Play this card to immediately void all rules you were taught in Economics 101.
cards.lore: Reality is what we imagine it to be. I imagine you're all being scammed.
cards.gradeReason: Instant embodiment: you know exactly who you ARE the moment you read it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Frantic yellow rabbit with frying pan explodes through economics textbook. Style: ink + watercolor. Subject: FrizzleBob mid-chaos. Mood: anarchic glee.

cards.power: The Unknowable Real – Target player realizes their senses are liars and skips a turn staring into the void.
cards.lore: The true objective reality. You can't see it, touch it, or understand it. So stop pretending you do.
cards.gradeReason: Knockout if you know Kant; needs one line of setup for everyone else.
cards.artworkPrompt: Dark tentacled cosmic horror looms; badger peers through doorway. Style: ink wash. Subject: Noumena vs. curious animal. Mood: existential dread.

cards.power: Warped Processing – Convert raw, terrifying truth into a comforting, structured lie using Time and Space.
cards.lore: Your brain adds time and space just so you don't lose your mind. Life is a constant act of desperate imagination.
cards.gradeReason: Explains Kant's categories of perception; describes brain mechanism rather than inviting performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Pig in steampunk goggles sees cute village while monsters lurk behind. Style: watercolor. Subject: perception filter device. Mood: blissful ignorance.

cards.power: Analytical Model – Test your geopolitical theories against the future. If wrong, fake 10 damage.
cards.lore: How do we know the model works? It predicts the future. We're testing theories against reality, exactly like an AI system.
cards.gradeReason: Analytical framing; compares deck to AI prediction. Describes, doesn't invite.
cards.artworkPrompt: Squirrel points at chaotic chalkboard of graphs, kites, math. Style: ink + watercolor. Subject: reality theory analyst. Mood: manic certainty.

cards.power: Inner-Marriage Monopoly – Combine your banks to mitigate risk when kinge default on their war loane.
cards.lore: Merchants needed to move wealth without getting robbed. So they invented a club, trusted only each other, and laid ths trap.
cards.gradeReason: Clear role; font artifacts ('kinge', 'loane', 'ths') indicate rendering corruption in source.
cards.artworkPrompt: Three fat gold-draped frogs sit atop coin mountain. Style: ink wash + gold watercolor. Subject: medieval banking cartel. Mood: smug complacency.

cards.power: The Firet Counterfeit – Create wealth out of thin air. Double your resources without lifting a finger.
cards.lore: I promise to give your gold back. The greatest trick ever played was convincing peasante that a piece of paper was as heavy as gold.
cards.gradeReason: Font artifact ('Firet') noted. Role crystal clear: you are the original grifter and you know it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Smug fox in vest hands scroll to stunned bear farmer. Style: watercolor. Subject: first paper currency moment. Mood: confidence game.

cards.power: Syetemic Panic – If 15 million in receelta aeks for 10 million in gold, the Illusion shatters. Game over.
cards.lore: The fatal flaw of the fractional grift. If everyone etops believing at the exact same time, the magic dies.
cards.gradeReason: Font artifacts noted ('Syetemic', 'receelta', 'aeks', 'etops'). Mechanism is iconic and immediate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Panicking sheep stampede toward bursting bank vault door. Style: dynamic ink + watercolor. Subject: fractional reserve collapse. Mood: systemic terror.

cards.power: Royal Hubris – Refuee to pay your war debts. Trigger the Central Banking Aaeaesine.
cards.lore: Kinge thought they had the power. They didn't realize the bank cartels would juet fund their brothers to overthrow them.
cards.gradeReason: Font artifacts throughout ('Refuee', 'Aaeaesine', 'Kinge', 'juet'). Great concept, heavy corruption.
cards.artworkPrompt: Roaring lion with crown confronts hooded monk bearing bill. Style: ink + watercolor. Subject: defaulting medieval monarch. Mood: hubris about to collapse.

cards.power: 10% Reserve – Lend out $4.5 million you don't have. Tell the public it's perfectly logical.
cards.lore: You put in 5 million, the bank lends out 4.5 million. The correct answer isn't 0.5 million total—it's 9.5 million total. It makes no sense, but it rules the world.
cards.gradeReason: Role clear but the mathematical explanation in lore makes it explanatory rather than performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Suited weasel juggles cash while confused mouse stares at floating coins. Style: watercolor + ink. Subject: fractional reserve banker. Mood: cheerful fraud.

cards.power: Fiat Skyscraper – Create money from nothing to build massive cities.
cards.lore: How did the Bank of China and ICBC become the largest in the world? They didn't wait for deposits; they printed reality into existence over 20 years.
cards.gradeReason: Specific China banking example reads as informational; lore teaches rather than invites.
cards.artworkPrompt: Panda in hard hat pulls skyscraper from magic top hat showering banknotes. Style: watercolor. Subject: fiat money construction boom. Mood: impossible scale.

cards.power: Illusion of Value – Maintain poverty to force all other players to work.
cards.lore: If everyone had money, no one would work. Poverty isn't an accident; it's a threat designed to make you hustle because real value is your labor.
cards.gradeReason: Darkest role in the deck so far. You immediately know who you're being asked to embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Bulldog enforcer holds SCARCITY sign while raccoons cower. Style: stark ink + watercolor. Subject: poverty as control mechanism. Mood: institutional menace.

cards.power: Food Waste Reality – Reveal that starvation is a logistical choice, not a resource limit.
cards.lore: Go to a garbage dump in Beijing. Food isn't scarce. Hunger is an artificial crisis enforced by an economic model that demands you believe in limits.
cards.gradeReason: Compelling reveal but the Beijing example grounds it in explanation rather than action.
cards.artworkPrompt: Raccoon discovers overflowing dumpster full of fresh fruit in city. Style: watercolor. Subject: food abundance amid manufactured scarcity. Mood: absurd revelation.

cards.power: Community Flourishing – Spend all your wealth to maximize your reputation. All players heal to full.
cards.lore: For most of human history, if you struck it rich, you didn't bury it—you fed the village. Collective happiness was the only happiness.
cards.gradeReason: The ultimate counter-move to hoarding. You know exactly what you're enacting and why.
cards.artworkPrompt: Wolf, bear, rabbit, fox feast together at overflowing table in forest. Style: warm watercolor. Subject: communal celebration feast. Mood: joyous abundance.

cards.power: Blood Money – Use currency to symbolically apologize for a debt that can never be repaid.
cards.lore: Before trade, money had no daily use. It was purely symbolic—a way to say I'm sorry I killed your cousin, please don't start a blood feud.
cards.gradeReason: Brilliant historical reframe; needs the anthropological context to land its punch.
cards.artworkPrompt: Badger offers coin bag to grieving deer family. Style: ink wash + grey. Subject: wergeld / blood debt payment. Mood: solemn reckoning.

cards.power: Ultimate Punishment – Remove a player from the community. Worse than death.
cards.lore: The concept of the individual didn't exist. You were part of the whole. Being banished to exist alone was the supreme nightmare.
cards.gradeReason: Pre-individual punishment as the ultimate horror. Immediately performable, viscerally understood.
cards.artworkPrompt: Dog walks alone into dark forest tunnel, village lights behind. Style: ink. Subject: banishment from community. Mood: existential desolation.

cards.power: Generational Wealth – Dig a hole, bury your joy, and save it for offspring who will resent you.
cards.lore: Today, if you get rich, you lock it in a vault and tell no one. We traded the feast for the bunker.
cards.gradeReason: Perfect foil to The Collective Feast but sits in descriptive mode rather than full embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Wild-eyed wolf digs hole to bury treasure chest under night sky. Style: ink + dark watercolor. Subject: compulsive wealth hoarding. Mood: paranoid isolation.

cards.power: Zero Agency – Accept that fate is random. Roll a dice; whatever happens, it's not your fault.
cards.lore: The ancients knew humans had no real control. Gods of Fate, Fortune, and Anger controlled the board. You just hoped they didn't notice you.
cards.gradeReason: Liberation through surrendered agency. Players immediately understand the polytheistic escape hatch.
cards.artworkPrompt: Giant cosmic hand reaches from clouds toward tiny confused goat. Style: watercolor. Subject: arbitrary divine fate. Mood: absurd relief.

cards.power: Divine Vengeance – Punish any player who gets too rich or too cocky.
cards.lore: If you made too much money, the gods would punish your pride. So people just enjoyed life instead of grinding themselves to dust.
cards.gradeReason: Clear enforcer role; the anvil-meets-peacock visual carries it but concept needs the polytheism chapter.
cards.artworkPrompt: PRIDE-labeled anvil smashes down on strutting peacock in golden light. Style: dramatic ink. Subject: divine punishment for excess. Mood: karmic inevitability.

cards.power: Flourishing – Since tomorrow isn't promised, live today at maximum velocity.
cards.lore: If you have no control over your ultimate fate, all you can do is seize the day. Flourishing over mere pleasure. The ancients were superior.
cards.gradeReason: Philosophical concept that instantly becomes a performance directive. Deer on storm-lit cliff nails it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Stag rears triumphantly on storm-lit cliff, lightning behind. Style: bold watercolor. Subject: Aristotelian flourishing. Mood: defiant vitality.

cards.power: System Reset – When people realize their misery isn't their own fault, they organize.
cards.lore: Polytheism allowed humans to blame external forces, which made collective rebellion possible. Power couldn't allow that to continue.
cards.gradeReason: Describes the mechanism by which power suppressed polytheism. Informational rather than performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Army of small animals with shields and torches charges a dark monster. Style: ink + stormy watercolor. Subject: mass collective rebellion. Mood: rising fury.

cards.power: The Synapse Cult – Convince target player they are nothing but memories and genes.
cards.lore: The modern worldview: you are just synapses reacting to experiences. Therefore, any misery you feel is entirely your personal problem to fix.
cards.gradeReason: Names the mechanism (Synapse Cult) but describes ideology rather than inviting embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Monkey trapped inside brain-shaped cage lit with neural pathways and DNA strands. Style: scientific watercolor. Subject: reductive neuroscience worldview. Mood: imprisoned.

cards.power: Internalized Blame – Disable collective action. Player must spend 3 turns trying to fix themselves.
cards.lore: Why does power love science? Because it isolates you. If you're depressed, you blame your brain, not the banking cartel that stole your future.
cards.gradeReason: The mechanic (3 turns of self-repair) is sharp; needs setup from the chapter's framing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Elephant carries enormous boulder on back in heavy rain, alone. Style: grey watercolor. Subject: internalized systemic blame. Mood: crushing isolation.

cards.power: Authority Dependency – Pay to feel worse. Target player becomes dependent on authority to process normal human sadness.
cards.lore: The system isn't designed to cure you. It's designed to replace your parents, your friends, and your nature walks with a dependent authority figure.
cards.gradeReason: Darkly funny role; the snake-on-couch visual carries it well. Needs slight satirical frame.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cobra in glasses holds clipboard as anxious mouse lies on therapy couch. Style: satirical ink. Subject: authority dependency via therapy. Mood: clinical absurdity.

cards.power: The Nature Walk – Go outside. Talk to a friend. Heal for free.
cards.lore: What actually cures sadness? Walking in the woods, resting, and talking to a buddy. Naturally, this is highly discouraged by the medical establishment.
cards.gradeReason: Punchline card of the chapter. Simplicity IS the joke. Immediately embody the radical act.
cards.artworkPrompt: Bear walks through sunlit autumn forest, free and alone. Style: luminous watercolor. Subject: nature as forbidden cure. Mood: serene rebellion.

cards.power: Wealth Destroyer – Periodically burn the economy to remind the peasants that money is scarce.
cards.lore: Why do markets crash? If there's too much money, you might stop working. Crisis is a controlled burn to keep you desperate.
cards.gradeReason: Controlled-burn mechanic is clear; role is performable once you accept the premise.
cards.artworkPrompt: Money tornado destroys rabbit and mouse houses in cheerful neighborhood. Style: dynamic watercolor. Subject: engineered economic collapse. Mood: deliberately orchestrated chaos.

cards.power: Resource Burner – Destroy actual wealth (lives and infrastructure) to justify the printing of fake wealth.
cards.lore: Wars aren't fought over scarce resources. They are fought to destroy resources, maintaining the illusion of scarcity.
cards.gradeReason: Counter-intuitive war thesis is intellectually compelling but reads as a lecture, not an invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Two rhinos charge each other while vulture counts gold coins above. Style: dramatic ink. Subject: war as resource destruction mechanism. Mood: profiteering carnage.

cards.power: Pointless Labor – Dedicate your finite life to extracting infinite pixels.
cards.lore: You play World of Warcraft to endlessly labor for fake currency because the real world trained you that work equals value. It's the exact same engine.
cards.gradeReason: Every gamer feels this in their bones. Immediate, universal, performable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Hamster on treadmill playing WoW on PC, coins piling up on screen. Style: chaotic digital ink. Subject: gamified pointless labor. Mood: compulsive futility.

cards.power: Apathetic Coping – Neutralize revolutionary potential by providing infinite digital dopamine.
cards.lore: Incapable of collective action and convinced you are the problem? Just play video games and watch porn all day. The system says Thank You.
cards.gradeReason: Bold lore but the adult content mention complicates table play in mixed settings.
cards.artworkPrompt: Sloth slouched on couch with controller, building burning in window behind. Style: dark watercolor. Subject: apathy as systemic tool. Mood: comfortable collapse.

cards.power: State Bullying – Hand 5-year-olds to 10-year-olds to be beaten into submission. In Architects Daughter.
cards.lore: The first free public school was in Sparta. Why? Because they needed mindless warriors, and you build those by institutionalizing trauma early.
cards.gradeReason: Shocking name, immediate historical role. You know exactly what you're performing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Muscular armored wolf towers over puppy soldiers in Spartan barracks. Style: blood-spatter ink. Subject: Spartan state education through trauma. Mood: institutionalized brutality.

cards.power: Compulsory Duty – Educate the youth perfectly so they don't flinch when the state demands their blood.
cards.lore: The Aztecs were the second society with mandatory public education. Another war machine dedicated to defeating neighbors and sacrificing its own.
cards.gradeReason: Specific historical parallel; Aztec context isn't universally known, needs the chapter setup.
cards.artworkPrompt: Jaguar warrior-priest teaches ducklings at pyramid steps below fiery sky. Style: dramatic watercolor. Subject: Aztec compulsory education as sacrifice prep. Mood: ceremonial dread.

cards.power: The Obedient Soldier – Ring a bell to condition biological functions. In Architects Daughter.
cards.lore: The blueprint for modern schooling. The Prussians didn't want thinkers; they wanted soldiers who obeyed orders without hesitation. You sit in their desks today.
cards.gradeReason: Every person who went to school has sat in this desk. The bell rings and you know.
cards.artworkPrompt: Eagle officer in Prussian helmet rings bell at rows of piglet students. Style: satirical ink. Subject: Prussian military education model. Mood: conditioning as architecture.

cards.power: Anxiety Inducer – Separate the child from its protector to maximize vulnerability. In Architects Daughter.
cards.lore: Why aren't parents allowed in the classroom? Because a child with a parent feels secure, and a secure child questions authority.
cards.gradeReason: Emotional revelation; needs the chapter's emotional buy-in to hit full force.
cards.artworkPrompt: Kangaroo mother torn from joey by robotic claw, both crying. Style: painful watercolor. Subject: parental separation as educational control tool. Mood: institutional violence.

cards.power: False Authority – Extract trust from terrified, isolated children. Architects Daughter.
cards.lore: Once stripped of parental protection, the anxious child has no choice but to trust the stranger at the front of the room. The brainwashing begins.
cards.gradeReason: Clear role with emotional depth; needs the full chapter context to land properly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Imposing owl stands at podium; frightened mouse child sits alone below. Style: stark dramatic ink. Subject: false authority over isolated child. Mood: coercive dependency.

cards.power: True Experience – Learn by doing. Anyone can become anything. Architects Daughter.
cards.lore: For most of history, if you wanted to be a doctor, you found a doctor and washed their floors until they taught you. Competence through reality, not tests.
cards.gradeReason: Counter-model card; shows the alternative but performs as a foil, not a first mover.
cards.artworkPrompt: Raccoon apprentice scrubs laboratory floor happily while badger mentor experiments above. Style: warm watercolor. Subject: apprenticeship as true education. Mood: joyful competence.

cards.power: The Credential Trap – Spend 20 years in a simulated environment and pretend it equals wisdom.
cards.lore: The modern system says smart people get degrees and stupid people wash dishes. It's a lie designed to sort compliant workers, not foster brilliance.
cards.gradeReason: Widely relatable satire; clear role that resonates immediately for most players.
cards.artworkPrompt: Poodle in graduation cap perches atop giant stack of books holding diploma. Style: satirical ink. Subject: credential trap. Mood: absurd ceremonial achievement.

cards.power: The System Bug – Ask Why? and risk immediate academic exile. In Architects Daughter.
cards.lore: Are you brainwashing us? If you're safe enough to ask the question, you're dangerous. School punishes questions and rewards regurgitation.
cards.gradeReason: One of the purest G1 cards in the deck. Single word trigger. System shatters on contact.
cards.artworkPrompt: Fox student raises hand, school explodes in blue energy around them. Style: explosive ink. Subject: the question that breaks the system. Mood: dangerous curiosity.

cards.power: Geography Lie – Implant false memories into a population to create a unified hive mind.
cards.lore: History class isn't about truth. It's the process of implanting a false memory so you believe The Nation is a living, breathing entity.
cards.gradeReason: Academic framing ('implant false memories', 'hive mind') reads as critique, not invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Fox teacher erases jungle map and replaces with NATION border map. Style: ink + watercolor. Subject: history as false memory installation. Mood: systematic replacement.

cards.power: Supreme Sacrifice – Convince individuals to die for a geographic concept.
cards.lore: Throughout history, you were from a village. You knew your neighbors. Now, you are forced to love Mother China or France and die for absolute strangers.
cards.gradeReason: Visceral and immediate. The flag-wrapped meat grinder image says everything.
cards.artworkPrompt: Flag-draped serpent-worm feeds tiny mouse soldiers into grinding machine. Style: horror watercolor. Subject: nationalist sacrifice as geographic abstraction. Mood: mechanical patriotic horror.

cards.power: Nothing Into Everything – Convince the masses that fictions are physical laws.
cards.lore: Alchemy wasn't a fake science; it was a political blueprint. Power is the capacity to turn an invisible concept into a chain around your neck.
cards.gradeReason: Brilliant metaphor but the goat-wizard describes power abstractly; invitation is indirect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Horned goat-wizard transmutes stones into glowing crown in purple smoke. Style: occult watercolor. Subject: power as alchemy of fiction into law. Mood: dark magical authority.

cards.power: Accident of Imagination – Realize the architects of the system were just as clueless as you are.
cards.lore: The great secret? It wasn't a master plan. It was an accident of the human imagination. We built our own prison because we didn't know what we were doing.
cards.gradeReason: The 'no conspiracy, just incompetence' reframe is intellectually interesting but purely descriptive.
cards.artworkPrompt: Confused mole engineer crashes self-built contraption into ground. Style: chaotic ink. Subject: unintentional systemic prison. Mood: clueless architects of catastrophe.

cards.power: The Centralized Truth – Eradicate local chaos and enforce a single, absolute reality.
cards.lore: The revolution of human thought. It wasn't just religion; it was the structural blueprint that made central banks and nation-states possible.
cards.gradeReason: Dense structural-historical thesis. Rewards slow reading but doesn't invite performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Single all-seeing eye in triangle radiates beam over diverse forest. Style: illuminated ink. Subject: monotheism as structural blueprint for centralized power. Mood: absolute singular truth.

cards.power: Soul Isolation – Disconnect from the collective. You are now entirely responsible for your own salvation.
cards.lore: Monotheism birthed the Individual. Once you had a personal soul to save, you were cut off from the tribe and ripe for institutional management.
cards.gradeReason: Chain of argument (monotheism → individual → management) reads as thesis, not invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Single orange fish swims away from blue school into vast dark ocean. Style: watercolor. Subject: individual soul isolation from collective. Mood: lonely spiritual responsibility.

cards.power: Infinite Ledger – Translate the concept of an infinite God into the concept of infinite Fiat currency.
cards.lore: If there is one God who creates the universe from nothing, then there can be one Central Bank that creates wealth from nothing.
cards.gradeReason: God → Central Bank parallel is one of the deck's best ideas. Needs the chapter to land fully.
cards.artworkPrompt: Nuns kneel before golden ATM labeled INFINITE FIAT in cathedral nave. Style: reverent ink. Subject: central bank as monotheistic institution. Mood: sacred financial absurdity.

cards.power: Paradigm Shift – Since reality is imagined, imagine a better one.
cards.lore: If the cage is made of imagination, the key is also made of imagination. Stop absorbing their fiction and start writing your own.
cards.gradeReason: Chapter closer; invitation is clear but slightly on-the-nose. Yellow rabbit with scissors is G1 energy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Yellow rabbit cuts through rainbow cage bars with giant scissors joyfully. Style: vibrant liberating watercolor. Subject: paradigm liberation through imagination. Mood: joyful escape.

cards.power: Cut Through Fiction – Permanently remove one Institutional Lie from the game board.
cards.lore: The system relies on you not noticing the seams. Find the seams. Cut them open.
cards.gradeReason: Tactile, immediate, embodied. The X-Acto blade is the deck's physical mascot. You know what to do.
cards.artworkPrompt: Badger slices institutional paperwork with giant X-Acto blade, bills flying. Style: sharp ink. Subject: epistemic sabotage via precision cutting. Mood: surgical rebellion.

cards.power: Rebuild the Collective – Bind two isolated players together, rendering them immune to Psychiatric Dependency.
cards.lore: They want you individual, guilty, and alone. Spite them by taping yourself to your neighbors.
cards.gradeReason: 'Tape yourself to your neighbors' is delightful direct instruction. Fully embodied, instantly played.
cards.artworkPrompt: Hedgehog and rabbit wrapped together in yellow masking tape, hearts floating. Style: warm ink. Subject: solidarity as physical binding. Mood: affectionate defiance.

cards.power: Ruin the Model – Discard the current Prediction Engine and force all players to embrace uncertainty.
cards.lore: Perfect predictive models are just traps with better PR. Spill the ink.
cards.gradeReason: Beautiful metaphor but 'Prediction Engine' is game-jargon that needs context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Black ink tsunami erupts from bottle drowning economic graph charts. Style: explosive ink wash. Subject: destroying predictive control models. Mood: chaotic liberation.

cards.power: Counterfeit Reality – If money is infinite, print your own. Duplicate any card in your hand.
cards.lore: They turned nothing into everything. It's time to steal their alchemy.
cards.gradeReason: Satisfying game mechanic and great metaphor; slightly meta but works well at table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Raccoon in bandana fires rebel pamphlets from exploding Xerox machine. Style: anarchist ink. Subject: copying their infinite creation powers. Mood: triumphant counterfeit.

cards.power: Draw Your Map – Ignore the Nation State's geography. Establish a new route between players.
cards.lore: They implanted a false memory of the world. Time to draw over it.
cards.gradeReason: Poetic directive but 'Ignore the Nation State's geography' needs setup from earlier chapters.
cards.artworkPrompt: Mole cartographer in pith helmet draws new map routes in sketchbook. Style: explorer watercolor. Subject: alternative geography as resistance. Mood: underground cartography.

cards.power: Cover Their Lies – Nullify an opponent's False Authority card by plastering weird art over it.
cards.lore: If the architecture is hostile, weaponize the aesthetic. Make it weird.
cards.gradeReason: Squirrel hanging upside-down plastering psychedelic art over corporate signage. You know the assignment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Squirrel hangs upside from lamp post pasting giant eye manifesto over official sign. Style: street art ink. Subject: art as counter-authority weapon. Mood: joyful defacement.

cards.power: Access Banned History – Look at the secret history discard pile and resurrect one lost truth.
cards.lore: School hides the truth. The library hoards it. Get the card, read the old magic.
cards.gradeReason: Clear and poetic but 'secret history discard pile' is deck-mechanics specific.
cards.artworkPrompt: Turtle holds glowing library card to dog; dusty secret archive opens behind. Style: luminous watercolor. Subject: library as access to forbidden knowledge. Mood: quietly radical.

cards.power: Summon Distractions – Overwhelm the authorities with a swarm of minor absurdities.
cards.lore: The system demands serious, rigorous compliance. Defeat it with a billion tiny, stupid jokes.
cards.gradeReason: Delightful concept but requires strategic context; the 'authorities' need to be defined.
cards.artworkPrompt: Swarm of tiny cartoon creatures march across official TAX document. Style: chaotic ink. Subject: absurdist distraction as resistance tactic. Mood: bureaucratic invasion.

cards.power: Cook For Friends – Abandon your shift at the Obedience Factory. Heal your entire party. Architects Daughter.
cards.lore: Hoarding wealth is an act of submission. A massive dinner party is an act of war.
cards.gradeReason: One sentence of lore and you know the political act you're committing. Pure G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Badger and fox cook outdoors in wild party; bank building smolders behind. Style: warm chaotic watercolor. Subject: communal feast as political rebellion. Mood: revolutionary joy.

cards.power: Tooch the Earth – Inetaolly cure the Internaoized Blame debuff. Arckitects Daughter.
cards.lore: The psychiatrist wants yeu on a Couoh. The earth wants yeu filthy and breathing. Choose the mud.
cards.gradeReason: Font artifacts noted ('Tooch', 'Inetaolly', 'Internaoized', 'Arckitects', 'yeu', 'Couoh'). Concept lands; execution corrupted.
cards.artworkPrompt: Shaggy dog explodes through muddy puddle in sunlight, pure joy. Style: kinetic watercolor. Subject: earth contact as antidepressant. Mood: muddy liberation.

cards.power: Interrupt the Lecture – Halt the current game phase until the aohority figure justifies their existence. Architects Daegher.
cards.lore: The single most dangerous word in the English language. Use it until the simulation breaks.
cards.gradeReason: Font artifacts ('aohority', 'Daegher'). Strong concept but relies on Architects Daughter mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Tiny bird holds WHY? sign facing colossal owl with glowing eyes at podium. Style: dramatic stark ink. Subject: dangerous question as power interruption. Mood: small vs. enormous authority.

cards.power: Sing Off-Key – Disrupt the Prussian bells. Erase all conditioned responses on the board. Arrvliscis Daughter.
cards.lore: They designed the heft to make you march. Yeu must design the noise that makes you dance.
cards.gradeReason: Font artifacts ('Arrvliscis', 'heft', 'Yeu'). Instruction 'Sing Off-Key' is pure G1 regardless of artifacts.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ram at drum kit smashes Prussian helmet cymbals; chains fly off in sound waves. Style: explosive music ink. Subject: joyous noise as conditioning disruptor. Mood: ecstatic release.

cards.power: Hear the Secret History – Become immune to the False Memory of History.
cards.lore: Once you hear the truth about the Central Bank, the Aztecs, and the Kantisn Noumena, you can never unhear it.
cards.gradeReason: Font artifact ('Kantisn'). Narrative identity card; rewards players who completed the whole deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Psychedelic rainbow rabbit ear floats in cosmic void. Style: surreal watercolor. Subject: FrizzleBob's ear as secret history antenna. Mood: kaleidoscopic revelation.

cards.power: Kick Down the Bank Doors – Destroy one Artificial Scarcity engine currently in play.
cards.lore: They told you it was a vault. It was just an imagination trap. Kick harder.
cards.gradeReason: Boot through bank door. Three words in the lore: 'Kick harder.' Instant G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Sneakered foot kicks through MERCHANT CARTEL bank door, gold coins exploding out. Style: kinetic ink. Subject: FrizzleBob's foot destroying artificial scarcity. Mood: cathartic destruction.

cards.power: Profit from Collapss – When the economy crashes (and it will), you win.
cards.lore: When you realize the crisis is a controlled burn, you stop panicking and start vlaying BINGO.
cards.gradeReason: Font artifacts ('Collapss', 'vlaying'). Meta-card needing game context; premise-before-play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Hyena waves BINGO card triumphantly as economy burns in background. Style: satirical ink. Subject: profiting from controlled economic collapse. Mood: knowing laughter.

cards.power: Ultimate Human Agency – Draw youl ewn way oot. Writs your own rule.
cards.lore: You ars not a synsps. You are not s subject of the Nation State. You are the architstc. Draw yeur escape.
cards.gradeReason: Severe font artifacts throughout. The blank card concept is the deck's perfect closer — G1 in intent, broken in execution. Urgent repair needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Empty cream postcard with pencil beside it on cutting mat. Style: minimal. Subject: ultimate blank invitation. Mood: open possibility.

verdict: Reality Redrawn is the flagship investigation deck in the Kayfabizarro catalog — 15 tightly structured chapters from Kantian epistemology through Prussian schooling to Eudaimonian rebellion, each unwrapping another layer of the manufactured sandbox. The thematic architecture is unmatched in depth and coherence; the One True Bank / Monotheistic Source parallel alone is worth the entry price. Critical weakness: severe font rendering artifacts on pages 2 and 15 corrupt lore and power text across 10+ cards, which is unacceptable for the Gumroad definitive release — fix before the next update. Table-ready: YES, with urgent font QA caveat.
blurb: For players who suspected the textbook was lying but couldn't prove it. 60 cards mapping the hidden architecture of money, school, and the nation-state — from Sparta to fiat to FrizzleBob. Start the investigation.

coverQA.coverNote: The cover doubles as the first card page which is risky but works here — each chapter gets its own page banner. Biggest risk: Kantian Noumena on page 1 is a cold open for players who don't know Kant. FrizzleBob as card 1 rescues it.

notes: Deck structured in 15 named thematic chapters (visible as page banner titles): Kult Klub intro / Infinite Fiat Scam / Artificial Misery / Before Individualism / Polytheism vs Synapse Cult / Blame Yourself / Treadmill of Distraction / Brainwash Factory Origins / Modern Classroom / Nation State Myth / Monotheism Blueprint / Epistemic Sabotage Tools / Analog Anarchy / Eudaimonia Deck / Kult Klub Initiation. Ten cards (29,31,32,33,34,36,53,54,55,56) carry 'Architects Daughter' cross-references in Power text — this deck combos with a companion deck. Font artifact corruption is heaviest on pages 2 and 15: page 2 has 'Kinge', 'loane', 'Firet', 'receelta', 'Syetemic', 'etops', 'Aaeaesine'; page 15 has 'Collapss', 'vlaying', 'youl ewn way oot', 'Writs', 'synsps', 'architstc' and more — decorative font baking failed QA on these pages. Page 1 is simultaneously the cover and first card page (no standalone cover). File identical in size (3,077,565 bytes) to RULES & HUB/media/kfb/ copy — ID suffix = InDesign production version. Previous prototype analysis existed as Kayfabizarro_Reality_Redrawn_WEB_v1.pdf.json (60 cards, score 8); this supersedes it as the definitive Gumroad release.
